title: Chicken Stuffed Peppers
description: Chicken Stuffed Peppers are made with a fajita style mixture that combines onions, garlic, tex mex spices and chicken, then oven-baked until soft and cheesy

source.rights: Feel Good Foodie. Functional content plus a link, for internal app testing. Not redistributed.

items.raw: 1 pound chicken breast (cut into bite-size pieces)
items.name: chicken breast (cut into bite-size pieces)

items.raw: 2 tablespoon fresh cilantro (plus more for garnish)
items.name: fresh cilantro (plus more for garnish)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375°F, and prepare the peppers by cutting them in half lengthwise and removing the seeds and membrane; set aside in a baking dish cut side up.

raw.text: Preheat oven to 375°F, and prepare the peppers by cutting them in half lengthwise and removing the seeds and membrane; set aside in a baking dish cut side up.
raw.name: Preheat oven to 375°F, and prepare the peppers by cutting them in half lengthwise and removing the seeds and membrane; set aside in a baking dish cut side up.

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onions and saute until they start to soften, about 2-3 minutes.

raw.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onions and saute until they start to soften, about 2-3 minutes.
raw.name: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onions and saute until they start to soften, about 2-3 minutes.

steps.text: Add garlic, chicken, chili powder, cumin and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.

raw.text: Add garlic, chicken, chili powder, cumin and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
raw.name: Add garlic, chicken, chili powder, cumin and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.

steps.text: Add rice, cilantro, lime juice, and stir together until heated through, about 2 minutes.

raw.text: Add rice, cilantro, lime juice, and stir together until heated through, about 2 minutes.
raw.name: Add rice, cilantro, lime juice, and stir together until heated through, about 2 minutes.

steps.text: Spoon the cooked chicken and rice mixture into the cut pepper halves, filling them to the top. Pour water into the baking dish to fill the bottom, being careful not to pour any water on the peppers.

raw.text: Spoon the cooked chicken and rice mixture into the cut pepper halves, filling them to the top. Pour water into the baking dish to fill the bottom, being careful not to pour any water on the peppers.
raw.name: Spoon the cooked chicken and rice mixture into the cut pepper halves, filling them to the top. Pour water into the baking dish to fill the bottom, being careful not to pour any water on the peppers.

steps.text: Cover baking dish with foil and bake until peppers are softened, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven, sprinkle with shredded cheese and return to oven to bake until cheese is melted, about 5 more minutes

raw.text: Cover baking dish with foil and bake until peppers are softened, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven, sprinkle with shredded cheese and return to oven to bake until cheese is melted, about 5 more minutes
raw.name: Cover baking dish with foil and bake until peppers are softened, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven, sprinkle with shredded cheese and return to oven to bake until cheese is melted, about 5 more minutes

steps.text: Serve immediately, topped with pico de gallo and sour cream, if desired.

review.reviewBody: Enjoyed these. Used up leftover roast chicken nicely. Could not find pico de gallo, substituted with canned Mexican tomato mix. Will make again
I had so much fun making these!! Super easy and delicious

Wonderful!! I used some precooked chicken breast that I always shred and keep in fridge for a good recipe. I also used quinoa in instead of rice. Soy yogurt and fresh cilantro on top and it was a winner! I’m going to make this many times.. it’s a keeper
Very good!! I added a small can of tomato sauce to the filling because my guy is Romanian and I thought it would be a nice addition. Thanks!
I think you missed out the tomato sauce/ paste in the recipe.  I see it on the video. :)
